title: Sur le tapis rouge  (On the Red Carpet)

segments.t: At the prestigious Cesars ceremony, Charlotte Gainsbourg warmly invites Mimie Mathy onto the red carpet. As photographers clamor for photos, Gabriel steps aside so that the two actresses can share the glamorous spotlight. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Mimie, viens faire des photos avec moi!
Tu es vraiment sûre, Charlotte?
Bien sûr, nous formons une équipe.
Les photographes attendent votre arrivée!
C'est un moment magique pour moi.
Tu mérites toute cette belle attention.
Je vous laisse briller ensemble!
Regarde vers les caméras, Mimie.
Je n'ai pas l'habitude de ça.
Souris, tu es magnifique ce soir!
Cette montée des marches est superbe.
Merci mille fois pour ce geste.
Le cinéma adore ta belle énergie.
Profitez pleinement de votre grand succès!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Mimie, viens faire des photos avec moi!
'Mimie, come take photos with me!' Charlotte welcomes Mimie warmly onto the red carpet. Dropping the subject pronoun turns the verb for 'come' into a direct, punchy command.
Tu es vraiment sûre, Charlotte?
'Are you really sure, Charlotte?' Mimie asks with humble disbelief. The informal 'you' form around 'this line' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Bien sûr, nous formons une équipe.
'Of course, we are a team.' Charlotte reaffirms their mutual respect. The verb meaning 'form' pairs naturally with the noun for 'team' in everyday conversation.
Les photographes attendent votre arrivée!
'The photographers are waiting for your arrival!' Gabriel points toward the flashing cameras. Gabriel uses the polite 'you' form alongside 'are waiting for' to keep a respectful professional tone.
C'est un moment magique pour moi.
'It is a magical moment for me.' Mimie takes in the glamorous setting. The descriptive adjective for 'magical' agrees in gender and number with its noun.
Tu mérites toute cette belle attention.
'You deserve all this fine attention.' Charlotte praises Mimie's artistic achievements. Notice how 'deserve' leads directly into the noun meaning 'attention'.
Je vous laisse briller ensemble!
'I leave you to shine together!' Gabriel steps back to give them full visibility. Gabriel uses the polite 'you' form alongside 'leave' to keep a respectful professional tone.
Regarde vers les caméras, Mimie.
'Look toward the cameras, Mimie.' Charlotte shares helpful tips for the photocall. Notice how 'look' leads directly into the noun meaning 'cameras'.
Je n'ai pas l'habitude de ça.
'I am not used to this.' Mimie reflects on the rare burst of gala spotlight. The verb meaning 'have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'habit' in everyday conversation.
Souris, tu es magnifique ce soir!
'Smile, you are stunning tonight!' Charlotte reassures her co-star with enthusiasm. The adjective meaning 'stunning' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Cette montée des marches est superbe.
'This red carpet arrival is superb.' Gabriel admires their shared public grace. The adjective meaning 'superb' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Merci mille fois pour ce geste.
'Thank you a thousand times for this gesture.' Mimie thanks Charlotte for sharing the limelight. The key noun here means 'times', anchored by its matching French article.
Le cinéma adore ta belle énergie.
'Cinema loves your wonderful energy.' Charlotte celebrates Mimie's enduring popular appeal. The verb meaning 'adores' pairs naturally with the noun for 'cinema' in everyday conversation.
Profitez pleinement de votre grand succès!

'Enjoy your great success to the fullest!' Gabriel encourages both actresses to relish the glory. The formal 'you' pronoun sets a courteous, professional distance around 'enjoy'. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

With generous warmth, Charlotte Gainsbourg and Mimie Mathy turn the red carpet into a moment of pure solidarity. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'come' and 'to do'. You'll catch them now. See you next time.
